function.name: read_file
function.description: Returns one page of one existing file as JSON. The page starts at line `offset` (1-based), `column` bytes into that line, and holds up to `limit` lines; a long line continues on the next page. The file's text is in `content` (null for bytes that are not text, with their count in `binary`; a smaller `limit` may isolate them). To continue, call again with `next.line` as `offset` and `next.column` as `column`; `eof` is true at the end of the file, and `changed` is true when the file changed since your last page of it, so read it again from the start. One file per call. No globs, no directories, no recursion. May be refused.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to read.

column.description: Byte offset into the first line, from a previous page's next.column. Default 0.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Replaces the entire contents of path with content. The file's directory must already exist; create it first with make_directory. This is not an edit, patch, or append — whatever was there is gone. Read the file before replacing it, every page until `eof` is true if you need all of its contents. Returns one of: applied; not written — nothing was written because the file exists and you have not read it, or it changed since you read it: read it, then write again; unavailable — do not retry; or outcome unknown — the write may have happened: do not retry it. The call's arguments, as JSON with `content` escaped, may be at most 61440 bytes, and a longer call is not run: you get an error giving its size, and the other calls in the reply still run. A large write, even within that limit, must be the only call in its reply; otherwise the reply may be refused, nothing in it is written, and the task ends.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to replace.

content.description: The complete new contents of the file.

function.name: list_directory
function.description: Lists one directory: one name per line, in byte order, each name a JSON string, with `/` after a directory's closing quote. Up to 1024 names per page, fewer when names are long; if there are more, the last line is `truncated — continue with after: "<name>"`, and calling again with that name as `after` returns the next page. Entries you may not see are simply absent, exactly as if they did not exist, up to the 65,536-name bound; a larger directory answers unavailable. The result has no count or total of anything. An empty result means there is nothing here you may see. Not recursive. May be refused: unavailable — do not retry.

path.description: Absolute path to the directory to list.

after.description: Return only names after this one: the name from the previous page's truncated line.

function.name: stat_path
function.description: Returns what is at one path as JSON: `kind` (file, directory, symlink or other), `size` in bytes, and `mtime_secs`, the last modification in seconds since the Unix epoch. A symlink is reported as itself and is not followed. Nothing else about the path is returned. May be refused: unavailable — do not retry.

function.name: make_directory
function.description: Creates the directory at path, and any missing directories above it. Returns one of: the directory exists — it was created, or was already there; unavailable — do not retry; or outcome unknown: the change may have happened; do not retry it.

path.description: Absolute path to the directory to create.

function.name: delete_path
function.description: Deletes the file or empty directory at path; with recursive true, a directory and everything beneath it. This cannot be undone. Returns one of: deleted; unavailable — do not retry; or outcome unknown: the change may have happened; do not retry it.

recursive.description: Delete a directory and everything in it. Default false: only a file or an empty directory.

function.name: task_agent
function.description: Gives a task to another agent and waits until it reports or its task ends. The other agent cannot see your files and you cannot see its files: put what it needs in the prompt, and ask for what you need in its report. Returns the start of its report and the path of a file holding all of it, or exactly one of: "not accepted, or its outcome is unknown; do not retry it"; "outcome unknown: the other agent may have the task; do not retry it"; "stopped"; "dropped"; "the agent was removed"; "the agent stopped responding"; "withdrawn"; "the task that asked for it ended"; "on hold — its agent or tasker was contained"; "the wait ended; the other agent's task may still run until it is closed; do not retry it"; or, outside an agent's own task, "unavailable — do not retry".

agent.description: The id of the agent to give the task to.

prompt.description: The task, with everything the other agent needs to do it.
